utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, good morning to you. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam. Mr. Oric, good morning to you. Can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen. I can follow the proceedings in my own language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, and also good morning to my learned friends of the Defence. My name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution. I am here together with co-counsel, Ms. Patricia Sellers, Ms. Joanne Richardson, and our acting case manager, Ms. Sanja Bokulic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben, and good morning to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, and good morning to my learned colleagues from the OTP. My name is Vasvija Vidovic, and together with Mr. John Jones I appear for Naser Oric. We have with us our legal assistant, Ms. Adisa Mehic, and our CaseMap manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic, and good morning to you and your team. Any preliminaries? Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No. It's just that for the record yesterday we filed a response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I was going to mention it. Okay. Thank you. Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, one matter in relation to that. We have received this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's -- in fact, it's a -- first of all, it's an application for leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Because it's late.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. And I would like to make a couple of remarks about this filing. We've only had the opportunity to briefly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can I stop you and suggest that you leave everything until Monday or Tuesday when we would have in the meantime received the other response, because we are in the same waters as you are and we have received the motion with no appendix, there's no attachments to it. We are fully aware that it is late.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's also too long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, it's 11 pages. I was reading it yesterday evening. I think it's 11 pages --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 15, yeah. I was reading yesterday evening between first course and second course. But let's leave it until we have also the other response and then we try and deal with the whole matter together, and our idea is to hand down a decision which will encompass all the different aspects.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, that's fine, Your Honour. Let me just say this, though, that firstly we would actually oppose leave being granted for the reason that actually the nature of this filing, it's so provocative, inflammatory, tendentious. It's really -- we say it's "full of sound and fury, signifying nothing," to quote the Bard; you'll have an opportunity to see that. And we say it's so unhelpful and so full of -- full of venom, really, you'll see. And it seems like the writer had an excess of spleen which he wanted to vent in this -- in this pleading. And you'll see that, Your Honours. You'll see it's extremely -- an extremely aggressive filing, and we disagree with practically everything that's in it. And the problem is, is that this -- if this is accepted, despite the fact that it is of this nature, the Prosecution have the last word on a lot of very contentious subjects which, of course, we disagree with and we need to come back on those matters. In terms of the length of the pleading, I would say if all the spleen were cut out, it probably would be about 10 pages, so you might consider redirecting a proper filing which is -- which doesn't have that, because Your Honour has suggested many times that we work in a spirit of cooperation, and to receive a filing which is -- in which every allegation we've made is absurd or extraordinary and where we're accused even of concealing a matter which we brought to the Prosecution's attention, which we brought to your attention, which we've been discussing for a year - this is the Banja Luka basement - for the Prosecution to point the finger at us and say we're concealing something is so absurd and so provocative that we're extremely unhappy with this filing, and we would either wish to file a rejoinder or what we may submit is that we'll show in the course of time with filings how wrong-headed this filing was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Wubben, what I'm going to do is take up Mr. Jones on what he's just suggested now, ask the Defence to file a rejoinder by Monday -- Monday when your -- end of business on Monday when your further response is due. That response is also going to put us in a better condition to be able to put everything in its perspective. But let me make one thing clear: That there comes a point in any matter similar to this where one cannot go any further and one has to live with the consequences of his or her actions or lack of action. So please do keep this in mind. And the consequences at this late stage of the proceedings may indeed be very serious. So keep what I'm telling you in mind before you make the final submissions on this. And I will adjourn on this matter until Tuesday, when we would have all the filings. Everything of course remains as it is for the time being. Your application for leave remains as an application for leave for the time being. And then we will decide everything after we hear what you have to say on Tuesday, and after us having had the opportunity also to see what your response is with regard to the fresh or the allegation of -- fresh allegation of violation of Rule 68 bis. Any further -- Madam Vidovic, any preliminaries on your part?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm pleased to inform you that I have in turn been informed by the registrar official that I had appointed to pick up the documents from Sarajevo, the documents that were examined by your calligraphic expert. They have been picked up and at least on the face of it, subject to correction, upon a superficial examination by -- of them by the officer herself, they seem to be in good order. So we leave it at that for the time being. Of course the Prosecution will have an opportunity to have a look at them because they are, after all, their documents, their property. And if there are problems, of course you will let us know. Let's bring the witness in, but she has to bring down the curtains. I think she has forgotten. It's a good thing I don't wake up tired in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, you can bring him in. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So good morning to you, sir. Welcome back.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are going to proceed with your examination and hopefully finish. Please try to be as brief as you can in your replies, in your answers, and to the point. Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I will wait until the sound effects are over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Witness, we were discussing yesterday a little bit of the skills that you had acquired during your JNA service, and I believe that you were informing us that you worked in a service that was based on the border or frontier. Could you just very briefly tell us as a member of the border service, did you learn how border guards should be stationed and how they should maintain that station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The border service consists of several groups of soldiers, one of which is always the patrol leader, the border patrol leader. The sections controlled were ranging from four to five kilometres, soldiers always went around at certain distances within -- of each other. And there were, of course, border posts directly on -- within --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were border guards directly on the border posts themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did border guards also learn how to relay messages among themselves since they were posted at such distances?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Border guards were not supposed to be too far from each other. They always had to be with invisible distance so they could assist one another.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Were there any skills such as use of radios, Motorolas, or other forms of communication that border guards were trained to use?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were such cases. There were sites designated at which group leaders could report in to let the others know their whereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Were border guards also trained in the use of binocular or any type of high-powered instrument to increase visibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I omitted to say that it was obligatory to have binoculars.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And were border guards trained in understanding land formations such as hills or valleys or recognising changes in land formations, if any?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One would undergo training before joining the border service. I went -- I underwent training in Skofja Loka and there were other places where one could go for three-month training before moving on to join the border service.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could you just very briefly explain to the Trial Chamber what was the essence of some of the training that you underwent before joining the border service.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The training was basically focussed on infantry matters and partially on APCs and tanks, which meant that one would undergo training within infantry ranks.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could I just inform the Trial Chamber I realise I left my microphone on when he responded at the last time if there's -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Isn't the main function of a border service to make sure that a border is not infiltrated by persons who don't belong inside of a territory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The border service -- border service already has its soldiers, whereas the other service, which is also a border service but it's different, is something that focuses on monitoring the border itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And by monitoring the border we mean deterring and, when necessary, stopping people from infiltrating territory. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I suppose it works the other way around, too, coming in and going out.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Escaped inhabitants, yes, could be another function.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is an excellent question. Yes, they do have observation posts.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, with your familiarity of the skills that you learned in the border service, could you confirm that that assisted you in maintaining the line in the village and the surrounding villages that you came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had few rifles, and that was why I informed others that they had to be aware of the fact that strong forces might appear and that they have to focus on observing. If strong groups were to suddenly appear without them -- seeing them in advance, we would definitely be defeated. In my opinion, the person who keeps a good lookout cannot be afraid even if confronted with ten people.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we can go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's go into private session for a short while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We are in open session at least. We had to be in private session because we were mentioning of course or dealing with areas which would have identified the witness. Yes, Ms. Sellers, which document is this?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe it's 908.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Sir, if I could ask you to once again look at the map, and I don't know whether you could designate in a circular fashion what is the region that you are referring to in your testimony as being Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the local commune of Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Well, thank you, sir. Because that's just where our confusion is. You've explained that there's a local commune, and at the same time we're hearing testimony of the Konjevic Polje region. And we'd like to be able to distinguish between the two, unless they coincide. So right now I'd asked: Could you show us or designate where is the Konjevic Polje region.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll explain to you now the centre of Konjevic Polje and the region of Konjevic Polje with its villages. Konjevic Polje --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, the -- if we could -- the technicians could zoom in that part of the map, please, so that we can follow better. Yes, I think that should be enough. Thank you. So for the time -- for the record, the witness has circled in red the point on the map described as Konjevic Polje. Yes -- to -- at 10.00 , between 10.00 and 11.00 to the north of Konjevici.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The villages of Konjevic Polje are Konjevici, Hrncici, Urkovici, Sandici, Lolici, Pobudje --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could we ask that the map be moved up just a tiny bit first.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I've drawn the lines correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, the witness has underlined in red all the villages he's just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. And one question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Eser has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I have a little bit of a problem. Now, you underlined Konjevic Polje, which is north of Konjevici. Do you have the map? You underlined Konjevic Polje --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He circled Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Circled Konjevic Polje. But Konjevici is south of Konjevic Polje. And when you indicated the region or the area of Konjevic Polje, you did not include Konjevic Polje itself. So is it that I understand that Konjevic Polje was not part of the Konjevic Polje area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The problems around Konjevic Polje have been occurring since 1979. There was an asphalt road leading from Konjevic Polje in the direction of Bratunac. At that time, it was called Konjevic Polje Tekija. That was the centre of Konjevic Polje. Konjevici is on a hill towards Banjevici. And when I see where it says "Konjevic Polje" on the map, I have to circle it because that's what the map says. But I know how far Konjevic Polje stretches. It's up to this junction here, in this area. That's the area really called Konjevic Polje, but it's all a little bit different on this map. If there's a problem, I can explain in detail, describe it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we can understand it as it is, especially since the line that you have now drawn beneath or below -- of Konjevici is precisely indicates Tekija, which is the outer limit of Konjevic Polje after 1979, as you mentioned it. Is that correct? Konjevic Polje Tekija? So it extends from --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Does that satisfy you okay, Judge? Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, would you, while we have the map in front of us, indicate where in the region of Konjevic Polje were the different groups maintaining a front line, if at all.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Hrncici they held the line in this area, as I've explained it before, this particular line. Urkovici covered this area here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we stop -- we need to explain this for the record. The -- with regard to the line guarded by Urkovici, the witness indicates an imaginary line between Grabovsko and Sandici to the east of Urkovici. With regard to Hrncici -- the other one was Hrncici, no? Yes, Hrncici, the witness - I can't read it properly - indicates a line from Ranonice in the direction of Panici. In the direction of Panici. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's called Pavici. It's a part of Hrncici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I am being contaminated by Ms. Sellers. I apologise to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: It's quite a fatal disease, heavy tongue, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead. We have mentioned two lines now. Go ahead, with the others, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pobudje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's Pobudje.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This unit with the group leader Ramo Omerovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. For the record, the witness indicates a curved line from the direction of -- from Kravica to the direction -- through Kamenica towards Burnice.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm looking at Pahljevici, but I cannot locate them here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, you have to go further up. If you see Konjevici, go -- move to the east one box and move north a box and a half. And you see it written horizontally along Drinjaca. It's further below Drinjaca. All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the line was there where you have pointed on the map now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So for the record, the witness draws a line across Pahljevici.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Are there any other front lines that one would consider being within the Konjevic Polje area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Another question with the map. You see up in the very far left-hand corner there's a town called Kamenica. Can you confirm to me that this Kamenica was not considered part of Konjevic Polje or any of the regions that you've indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, we have to zoom out. Yes, exactly. Zoom out and we're talking of -- until it comes to the map -- yes, all right. If you look at the map top left -- top left second and third square. Right at the top you see Kamenica. It's the second and third square. And on the top of those two squares there is the name "Kamenica."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the question is whether -- whether it's correct that Kamenica was never considered to form part of Konjevic Polje or any of the regions that you have indicated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Kamenica is very far away from Konjevic Polje and never formed part of Konjevic Polje. I believe it's some 10 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Can we zoom back in to the area of Konjevic Polje that we were dealing with before, please. Yes, yes, yes. Now, sir, look at Urkovici -- no, no. Keep it where it was, please -- no, where it was. Further up, further up, further up, yes. Stop, stop. Now, look, you can see Urkovici there. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can see Lolici just beneath Urkovici.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And if you go further down in the same box as Lolici you see Kamenice.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What about that? Is that a different Kamenica, Kameice, or is it Kramenice? Because it could also be Kramenice. What name is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the village of Pobudje. It is called Kamenice or Kamenica, just as the other one. There is not much of a difference in terms of the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm sure we'll find about a dozen others in other areas as well. So your question now -- there are two Kamenicas, and I would like to know which one you were referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Then, Your Honour, I would like to ask the witness -- I was referring, for purposes of the map, to the one up in the far left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now I want to ask the witness: The testimony that you've given over the past couple of days, when you refer to Kamenica, or that's how we saw it appear in our English transcript, which town were you referring to in terms of battles or attacks in Kamenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was referring to the village of Kamenica, not the town of Kamenica. The town of Kamenica is further away; it's not close at all. I meant Kamenica, the village of Pobudje, that's what I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That's quite helpful to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I believe we can remove the map for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us what were your duties within your unit. What function did you perform?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think we need to be a little bit more specific here, both as regards time and also the unit that you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was going to avoid the unit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes -- I suppose I reflect what you had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wanted to avoid maybe having the witness speak of the unit, unless that presents no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think it presents a problem. I mean, he was not ...

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, tell us what was your unit called, formally, informally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was called the group from Urkovici. You asked me about the function that I had. My role was to provide food. I told you that I had to take care of large numbers of refugees from Sandici, and we had to supply them with food. Even the children were involved because very soon we ran out of food. But I have to tell you that I regretted being in that duty because I felt really humbled by the fact that I did not have my rifle any longer, humiliated even, because I was unable to protect my family.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Can you tell me the duties of other people in the Urkovici group other than yourself.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean armed people, those who were armed of course had to stand guard to forewarn us of any impending attack and to seek assistance in case the attack is a fierce one. That was about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So those who had to seek assistance, would they travel to the different units in that area to ask for assistance, to bring the message that, We need help?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In such situations, since the people had to move from one village to another, it would happen that someone would go directly to others and then warn them that they needed to help. If they came across someone, that very often whoever set off in the direction of my village, he would then ask those people to alert others to send in help.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you have the use of any types of radios or Motorolas or communication equipment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had we had it anywhere, life would be much easier for us, but we did not use them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. You did not use them or you didn't have them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We neither had them nor used them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Isn't it true that Azem Rizvanovic was, in essence, your communication officer or person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. Azem Rizvanovic was a man deeply shaken by the events that he experienced as well as others in Glogova. He came to Urkovici via Popovici, and he was a very distressed man. I had the feeling that he was never really in his right mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll stop here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we'll have a 30-minute break starting from now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Witness, if Azem Rizvanovic did not function as communications person or officer, could you please tell the Trial Chamber then who did.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told you at the beginning that Azem Rizvanovic came from the direction of Glogova. He was a deeply traumatised man. He looked quite ill. He had a sister in my own village, and he stayed at her place throughout the combat activities in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop, stop, stop. I don't know if it's a matter of interpretation, but if it isn't and this is the style that you are going to adopt, you are going to be here Monday, if not also Tuesday. The question was a very simple one. Ms. Sellers told you: If it wasn't Azem Rizvanovic that functioned as a communications person - and you have already -- you already told her that he didn't do anything of the sort - then who did? This is the question. So if there was someone else who functioned as such in this position, please tell us. If there wasn't anyone, say there was no one. Otherwise, you keep on ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as far as I know, nobody was performing the duty of communications.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's exactly what I wanted to say, Your Honour. The witness did not accept ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. But let him finish before because I couldn't hear what you were saying and the interpreters couldn't hear what you were saying. So the answer is: There was no one, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, does that mean there was no one doing communications in the Urkovici group, or does that mean that there was no one doing communications with this area that you've described as Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, nobody did in Urkovici. And according to my knowledge, nobody did that sort of job in Konjevic Polje either.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: If no one did that job, are you saying that there might have been communications by Motorola or RUPs but it was not necessarily the function of any one person in that area during the 1992 time period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no communications with any sort of means.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Does that mean that there were no couriers, no people who took messages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no couriers either.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you know a person named Velija, and I believe his nickname was Elektrika?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Velija if you are referring to Velija Omerovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did he have a nickname of Elektrika?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was an electrician. As for his nickname, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Wasn't he a courier, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told you that I know nothing of couriers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Does that mean that you don't know whether Esad Selimovic was a courier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the man, believe me, Esad Selimovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And if you could just -- if I could beg your indulgence, would you tell us whether Sadik, who had a nickname of Vakunja [phoen], whether he was a courier at the time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean Sadik Hajdarevic, I know him, but I don't know anything about any couriers or about the nickname.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. So it's your testimony that there was neither radio communication nor courier communication among the different groups in the region that you've described as Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Prior to April 1992 when many of the people who we've discussed have become leaders in the region, was there a TO Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: There was no Territorial Defence organisation or office in that region, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Was one organised as a result of people like Velid Sabic, Vejiz Sabic, Enes Ibrahimovic in that area as of April 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we could just have the witness have the map again. I believe that would be Defence Exhibit 509.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it 509, Usher?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you for the correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I ask because he was marking on it -- and please do remind me at the end of this witness's testimony to have him sign the map. I haven't asked him to sign because I never know exactly where the camera happens to be focussing, so I will leave it until the very end.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Sir, if you would look at the map where we have what appears to be two roads, one coming up from Milici, the other going through the villages we've talked about, including Urkovici, and they meet at a crossroad prior to going up to what you've described as the town of Konjevic Polje. Was there ever a school near those crossroads?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question; I haven't understood it fully.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: My question was: Was there a school, an elementary school, or a school for learning near those crossroads?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Konjevic Polje there was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could you indicate for us on the map where that school was, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So one -- stop, stop. For the record, the witness draws a circle around a spot at 10.00 of Tekija below Konjevici on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, sir, you were asked the question I believe on direct examination in relationship to schools at times being used as military installations. Do you remember that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That school was not used as a military feature. Children attended school there until the 27th of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And after the 27th of April, did children attend schools -- school there, where you've indicated, after the 27th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the schools in the area, including the one in Konjevic Polje, closed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, was that school building, after it closed, was it ever used during the time period between April 1992 until the fall of Konjevic Polje for other reasons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The school was used for displaced persons and refugees until early August when Nurif's fighters arrived from Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And then what was the school used for after Nurif's fighters arrived from Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nurif's fighters, when they arrived from Tuzla, were given a part of the school, in my estimation a third to a quarter of the school, and the remainder stayed in tents put up around the school. The people from the area, Konjevic Polje, and there were few of those, they went to their family houses and their families and stayed there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So the fighters stayed in their own homes during this time period, April 1992 until the fall of Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not from April. You misunderstood me. I'm referring to August when Nurif's fighters arrived from Tuzla. Those of them who originated from Konjevic Polje - and that was a small number of them - they went home to stay with their families.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. So before Nurif's soldiers arrived, was the school used to house any of the fighters that came from other areas of Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if you would permit me one moment, I just would like to check the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir, where I'm confused is that you answered me when I asked: "So did the fighters stay in their own homes during this time period?" You said: "Those of them who originated from Konjevic Polje - and that was a small number of them - they went to their home to stay with their families." Are you referring to those men who came with Nurif Rizvanovic who didn't stay in the school but went home to stay with their families?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. You've testified that there were men from Sandici, fighters from Sandici, who were not in Sandici but who stayed, I believe, in Urkovici or in other towns. Did they stay in any special building, such as a school, or did they stay in people's homes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They stayed in other people's homes. Quite a few people from Konjevic Polje had gone abroad and their houses remained empty. They were with their families.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So the fighters were lodged in different homes, in residences, in the Konjevic Polje area, if that's what I can understand you to say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, other than when Nurif Rizvanovic's men used the school to billet his soldiers, was the school used for meetings among other fighters or soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Was the school used for people meeting -- other fighters from the region meeting with Nurif Rizvanovic and his soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to take you back now to May 1992. You've testified rather extensively on your direct examination - excuse me, I mean April 1992 - about having to turn over weapons to Serbs. And you referred that this occurred I believe in Sandici. Was that your testimony, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And you indicated by your testimony that you were caught there, and then I believe you went back to your home town and then you returned to turn over the weapons. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, let's continue, Ms. Sellers. In the meantime, that will be taken care of.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Sir, do you believe that we can stay in open session while we talk about this and the upcoming attack? I'll ask you because it depends on how you will express yourself for these answers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: But you've testified that a person named Munad -- Munib Sanic appeared that time when you were caught and that you were quite relieved to see him. Do you remember that testimony, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that testimony because I was left in the village on my own. When I saw that Munib Sabic was there, too, I felt easier because I was no longer alone.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. You've answered my next question, and I just wanted to know if it was Munid Sanic or Munib Sabic, and it's Munib Sabic, if I understand your last answer. You'll have to reply in the microphone, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether Munib Sabic is alive today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Do you know how he met his death, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you that I heard that when we arrived in Srebrenica he was killed in fighting around Srebrenica, but I don't know the precise location.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of job Munib Sabic held, if any?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Srebrenica, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry. I should have clarified that. I meant before the war or at the time period in April 1992 when you have indicated that you were with him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992, in April, he helped me. He had a lot of people from Sandici in Urkovici, and he looked after his people and the women and children, helping them to survive in that period.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, when you say that he had a lot of people in Sandici, do you mean that he had a group of people, men, women, and children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say group of civilians, in other words.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: These were refugees from Sandici who were staying in Urkovici. Is that what I'm to understand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And was he a type of leader of that group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not the leader of that group. How can I explain this? He was a man who was looking after them to help them survive.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would ask you to try and be more precise. Looking after them to help them survive, could you tell us what that means. What did he do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He collected food for the people from his village of Sandici.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Is that among the reasons that you knew him because you both had to collect food to assist others to survive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That wasn't the only reason. Munib Sabic and I had gone to school together in Kravica and we knew each other very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether Munib Sabic had bought guns on the black-market during this time period or prior to the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if we are in open session, I ask that this part be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Fair enough. I think we will do that. Yes, yes, I'm trying to see where -- which -- where we redact from. I think we better redact the whole question and answer. Page 42, line 20 -- line 20 to line [sic] 43. Yes, yes, yes, page 43, first line. I said line 43, that was a mistake. It's page 43, line 1. In the meantime, we can continue, and that will be taken care of. Microphones are off.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to be continuing a little bit with this incident, so I would ask again if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go into private session for a short while, and then it's easier.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Witness, you've just described this device of a bottle with a corn-cob that would then become an incendiary device. Was this used because you had so few weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And how long did it take to make the device, the bottle, the corn, and the ingredients?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: How many did you make to use on May 29th, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 20 bottles or so, maybe five or six extra ones. We had a crate full of beer bottles and five or six other bottles that the young men were carrying in their hands.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And where did you get the liquid material that you placed in the bottle?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go into private session for a short while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session, Ms. Sellers, and Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, you've agreed that using that device of the liquid in the bottles was in substitution for a weapon. Whose idea was it to use that type of device among your group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was my idea. I've already said so, that I can -- I will always regret the fact that I had handed over my rifle and was unable to defend myself and those who were -- my family, as the others could.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did others in your group or other groups who were also unarmed didn't think that was a good device for them to use since they didn't have weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had -- it was just a split of a second in which we had to decide, to make a decision, and I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I agree. My question was: Did others in your group also think that was a good idea to have that type of device since they didn't have a weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When this particular fighting was over, they agreed that it was a good choice.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And did they ever use that good choice of weapons at other attacks or counter-attacks or incidents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No more opportunities arose for us to use them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So that was just a one-time use by your unit, your group, of incendiary devices. That's your testimony, right, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you've testified of the presence of Mr. Munib Sabic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So I would now ask that the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit ERN number 03592985. Your Honours, this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For your direction, Ms. Vidovic, this is the last document on the first list that was submitted by the Defence, all right, which was discussed yesterday -- the day before, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to say that this is a document, 33-page document. The original is dated on the 9th of December, 1994. It's a list of candidates for receiving different medals and awards. The document has come into the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor. If we would just turn to the first page of the document, it's not that I want to concentrate on this page but I'd like to just give some information so that the witness will understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Sir, I believe that you have the B/C/S now, and I'll just repeat that this is a document that on its face says it comes from the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, 8th Srebrenica Operations Group command, dated Srebrenica 9th of December, 1994, entitled "proposal for awarding declarations to the members of the 8th Operational Group," and it's directed to the 2nd Corps command Tuzla, department for morale. And the first line is: "Pursuant to consultation with the assistant commander for morale at the meetings held on November 14th, 1994, and November 28th, 1994, as well as based on the units' proposals for awarding incentives," and then it continues in a preliminary manner to describe its purpose. I would just briefly direct your attention to the last page of the document. And one will note in the English version that that would be page 61; in the B/C/S version it's actually the next-to-the-last page. I'm sorry, page 60.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In English, yeah, exactly, we have 60 pages.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And I just draw your attention that it's signed -- it says: "Commander Brigadier Naser Oric." There is a stamp that is affixed to it, along with a signature. Sir, have you been able to follow that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. If you're asking me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now ask you to turn to ERN for the B/C/S version 03593017, and I believe it says page 33, 33 in the upper right-hand corner of the B/C/S version. Within the English version, we're on page 28 of 60. And I would direct your attention where under section A, exemplary service medals, it states the following: "Munib, son of Mujo Sabic, 284th iblbr," and it says "posthumously." Now, sir, you've indicated to us that Mr. Sabic, to your knowledge, is deceased and was deceased prior to 1994. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said that he got killed in 1994 in some fighting around Srebrenica, if you've understood me well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You forgot your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Well, sir, thank you for the correction. So if I can just look at the transcript, he's deceased prior to the end of 1994. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I honestly can't follow now. Why isn't it correct? When was he killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was killed in 1994. I attended his burial. He was a very close friend of mine. I've told you so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So he was killed before the end of 1994. That was the question. Yes. All right. Okay. So let's proceed. So it must have been a problem of translation I think or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Sir, can you just follow as I'll read where it says: "Mujo, son of" -- pardon me, before we get to that. You've indicated before that you did your JNA service and that you're familiar with military. Based upon your knowledge of the military, are awards, medals, or commendations at times given out to soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And during wartime, are soldiers often awarded medals or commendations for bravery for their actions in war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is, indeed, the case, but I don't know which soldiers you're referring to right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm speaking in general, just pulling upon your experience. And then I would ask you that soldiers, in particular during wartime, who might receive medals, is it possible that those medals are awarded to soldiers after they die, after at times they've been killed in battle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I found out about it in 1995, as I went around to Tuzla, that something of the sort had been awarded.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So it would be thoroughly misleading for anyone to suggest that -- to suggest that a soldier can only receive a medal or a commendation if they are alive. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. -- Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I just find that thoroughly misleading. It is surely inaccurate. I don't see how the witness can comment on whether it's misleading. That implies a whole set of other circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the witness as someone who is familiar with military procedures and awards can say whether they would be thoroughly misleading or not. Is that -- let's just say "misleading."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If the witness has already told you that when he went to Tuzla and came to know that such awards, posthumous awards were being made or granted, he is actually answering your question at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I agree. But it has been suggested at times to other questions it's misleading. I want to know from his experience: Wouldn't that be misleading to suggest that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's told you -- even if he didn't know about it before, he came to know about it --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Absolutely fine. We'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: We'll come to the first line of the material in front of you. "Munib, son of Mujo Sabic, was born in Urkovici, municipality of Bratunac, 1958. He was a driver, married with three children. He joined the RBiH armed forces on the 15th of April, 1992. He joined the 114th Konjevic Polje Brigade," and then it goes on to say in describing him. "He took part of the organisation of the resistance against the enemy in the territory of Konjevic Polje. Local community, chiefly having been engaged in acquiring and purchase of weapons for his village, since he worked as a driver in the Vihor company of Bratunac." It goes on to say: "Until his death, he took part in all the critical and strenuous actions that were performed by his unit. He especially stood out on the 29th of May, 1992, when a tank and infantry attack was launched from the direction of Kravica against the free territory of Konjevic Polje." Now, Witness, in this -- in particular, this last part that I've read that refers to the attack, this confirms to the testimony that you've just given the Trial Chamber. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I've told you that Munib Sabic did not have any weapons, that he was with me, and it was with those devices that we tried to defend Konjevic Polje or, rather, the area of Lolici.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. It goes on to say: "The free territory of Konjevic Polje in order to relieve a blockade of the road that our forces had blocked for the aggressor two days before. When the situation turned critical, i.e., when our lines on the road between Kravica and Konjevic Polje near Sandici were put at risk of being broken, he left his radio transmitter, took his automatic rifle, and went to the rear of the enemy on his own initiative. In a hard and merciless close encounter with the Vukovar volunteers who had come to the aid of their brothers in Kravica, he managed to kill eight Chetniks." Now, Witness, you've testified about volunteers from Vukovar. Would you agree with what's written here in terms of their presence during that time period and, in particular, during that attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree about this part concerning the -- those from Vukovar. However, I would not agree with the part mentioning the man, Munib, as carrying a rifle and a radio because I know for a fact that he did not have a rifle on him. And this -- I find it really hard to read this.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: If you could just bear with us a little bit longer, I would like to continue in reading it. And I appreciate your answer. It says that he: "Managed to kill eight Chetniks from whom he took the weapons and the equipment and brought it all to his fellow combatants, who had until then been fighting bare-handed." Now, do you agree that you and your group were fighting bare-handed, and that's why you, as a matter of fact, made the incendiary devices that one could commonly refer to as Molotov cocktails?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my earlier testimony I said that there were about 50 rifles among those who came to assist us, whereas Munib Sabic, I, and several other young lads who were under 18 only had the devices that we ourselves made.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So would you think that in describing someone for the award of a medal, would you agree with me that there's been a little bit of puffery in this description?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course one exaggerates. I don't know who issued these awards, who authored the text. I have no idea really.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Would you also agree that the essence of the attack on the 29th of May, 1992, the presence of the Vukovar fighters, the presence of Munib Sabic, and the fact that there was a successful resistance on the part of your group, that that is true, as captured in the text?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We put up good resistance, that's true; that's why they were unable to go through. We had about 50 armed men, I told you, who were defending the passage.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: The same text, it then refers to the: "Eight enemy soldiers remain lying dead in our territory as proof of the aggression against Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina from another state." And adds testimony about "a hero who by his personal act turned the tide of the battle to our favour." Now, you've testified about volunteers coming from outside of Bosnia. Does this reflect a bit of your testimony concerning those volunteers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Bego Muminovic brought some of the documents which belonged to those who were killed, and one could see that they were from the area around Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, when someone volunteers to go into military service, as the people from Vukovar, are they therefore not considered to be soldiers, just volunteers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are considered to be soldiers and volunteers alike.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Wouldn't you agree with me that volunteering, in essence, just represents a way that you can become a soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A soldier appears to be a soldier because he is well-armed and equipped, whereas when you say "a volunteer," it only denotes a person who joined something -- volunteered to become a part of something.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: The volunteers that came from Croatia with Nurif Rizvanovic, were they soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And the volunteers from Vukovar were soldiers; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Soldiers, volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And is it still your testimony that you're completely unaware that Munib Sabic was engaged in acquiring or purchasing weapons in the time period of April 1992 or therearounds?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I claim that this is definitely not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would just like to read down one or two more lines where it says -- as a matter of fact, just the phrase: "Since then Munib was intercepting Chetnik radio communications." Did you know whether Munib Sabic in 1992 intercepted Chetnik radio communications?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. We did not have any radio-set in Urkovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me if I want to belabour the point a bit. So can I understand you to be saying that there was no ability to intercept Chetnik VRS communications in Urkovici during this time period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no communication over any communications devices.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you have transistor radios?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had transistor radios, but we had nothing to power them on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So lastly, is it also your testimony that in the entire Konjevic Polje area that you've described, there was no intercepting of radio communications from Chetniks or the VRS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was none.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would ask that this document be given a P number and moved into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, Ms. Sellers. So this -- let me describe this document first. It consists in the Serbo-Croat version of pages starting from 03592985 up to and inclusive of 03593050, and a corresponding translation thereof into English consisting of 60 typewritten pages. This document is being tendered, received, and marked as Prosecution Exhibit P?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 595, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: P595. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, if I can paraphrase a bit. In some of your answers you've indicated that there appears to be a before and an after when Nurif Rizvanovic arrives in the area of Konjevic Polje. My question is then: Did things change militarily upon the arrival of Mr. Rizvanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did Mr. Rizvanovic bring not only uniformed, armed men, but hope into the region of Konjevic Polje for Bosnian Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did he also bring a concrete example that the 2nd Corps in Tuzla wanted to have military contact reinforcements with the Konjevic Polje region, at least?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I happened to be in Konjevic Polje when Nurif Rizvanovic arrived with his men, with his fighters. I heard him say that he came there with the intention of being commander of the Drina region.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Do you know whether he had been sent by the 2nd Corps in Tuzla officially to be in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly what he said.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And if you would just confirm for me, he came equipped with arms, with uniforms, and with military apparatus. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Rizvanovic is originally from the Glogova area. Do you know whether he knew Ejub Golic prior to this time, prior to midsummer 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that they knew each other.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So when Mr. Rizvanovic arrives, does he bring with him military apparatus such as Motorolas, communication devices, ham radios, or any other type of device so that he can keep in contact with Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you that I really didn't see any communications centre or anything like that. But as for rifles and uniforms, I did see those, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Let's go back just a little bit before Mr. Rizvanovic comes, and we're in June of 1992. Did the men in your group, let's say in Bego Muminovic's group, or in Velid Sabic's group, Vejiz Sabic's group, Enes Ibrahimovic's group, did they know about fighters or groups in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one knew anything about Srebrenica, to the best of my knowledge, unless they kept it secret. But I didn't know anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did anyone in your group know of fighters in Suceska, Zulfo Tursunovic's fighters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's very far away. I learned about that when I arrived in Srebrenica. Suceska is far away from even Srebrenica, let alone from where we were.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And then lastly, did anyone during that time period, June 1992 and the different groups of fighters in Konjevic Polje, know about Ahmo Tihic's group from Kragljivoda?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Do you -- pardon me. Do you know someone named Dzemail Becirevic. Djazmel -- I might be mispronouncing that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dzemail Becirevic, that's the correct name, is from Hrncici.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Were you familiar with any role he played during this time period in 1992 in the Konjevic Polje area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The man was completely unarmed. I only saw him in passing from time to time but had no particular contacts with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So he wasn't one of the fighters, if I understand what you're saying, but he was completely unarmed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Although, you do agree that you don't have to have an arm to be considered fighter, because there were fighters who didn't have arms because there weren't enough arms to go around. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if that's how it was. It's possible if someone is killed for somebody else to take their weapon and continue fighting, so that could happen.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Sir, let's turn back to -- I appreciate your answer. Let's turn back to Mr. Becirevic. Did he play a political role in Konjevic Polje during this time period, or in the area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Do you know whether he was a member of the War Presidency in the area of Konjevic Polje or in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no War Presidency, especially not in Bratunac or Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Do you know whether he played any type of political or military role or as an authority in the area of Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no authorities in Konjevic Polje, only groups of men in the villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Sir, are you aware that Dzemail Becirevic went to Srebrenica in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Are you aware that Velid Sabic sent couriers to Srebrenica to make contact with Naser Oric in June 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing about any couriers, just civilians who may have happened to come looking for food.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Do you know whether Naser Oric came to the region of Konjevic Polje in June or early July of 1992 to see Vejiz Sabic or Velid Sabic or Mr. Becirevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally know nothing about Naser Oric, except that in 1994 when I arrived in Srebrenica I saw that man.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So, sir, would your answer be: No, that you didn't know that Naser Oric visited that area in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And did you ever see Mr. Becirevic in the area of -- in the area of Konjevic Polje, including all the different towns and hamlets, during that time period, in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Becirevic had a house in Hrncici uphill and also in Konjevic Polje -- no, not Konjevic Polje --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think this might be an appropriate time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's definitely more than appropriate. But before we do so let's redact, please, page 62, lines 10 and 11. Ms. Sellers, do I take it that you're not going to finish today?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that that is a correct assumption. But I would like to state that I have cut down, believe it or not, considerably and will be hopefully moving just a bit quicker during this next segment. But I anticipate that I will probably need the first segment of Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Monday. So if that is the case, do you think that you would be able to finish with your witness, say, Monday -- but on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry, do you mean the re-examination of this witness or the next witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. First re-examination of this witness and then the next witness. Because if you think that you would require the whole of Monday, then we need to review a little bit what we had -- next witness after this one, do you think you would be able to finish him in one day?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if Ms. Sellers finishes by the first break, as she said, depending on the further course of the cross-examination, based on the questions so far, I will need seven or eight minutes plus, depending on how the situation develops. But I will try to be as brief as possible, and I will attempt to finish with this witness by the end of Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The next witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We envisaged two days for Mr. Mustafic, including the cross-examination. We will try to complete his testimony in chief in about three hours, at the most -- three to four hours, which means that if we have two hours on the first day and two hours on the next ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Please correct me if I'm wrong, but does Defence counsel indeed plan then to finish the following witness by the end of Tuesday? That means that we cannot anticipate for the 30th --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, I told you. We will not be sitting on the 30th.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Okay. That's just for my understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. If you think that you will not be able to finish with the next witness, please tell me so that we will eliminate him and dedicate -- we'll finish with this witness on Monday, and then dedicate the rest of the time to thrash the -- completely, entirely, Rule 68 business on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No, we -- the witness, firstly, I believe might have even arrived last night, and we can certainly finish with him by next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's make an effort. Let's have a break, 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers. I hope you understood, Witness, that unfortunately we did not manage to finish with your testimony today but it should be over on Monday. In the meantime, you'll have an opportunity to enjoy the beautiful weather of The Hague over the weekend.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Sir, in your prior testimony on direct examination, you've been able to convey to the Trial Chamber the different locations that were visible from Urkovici. In those locations you included Siljkovici, Kravica. My question to you is whether you could see, either with the naked eye or binoculars, Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not see Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Had you ever been to the village of Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I've never been to the village itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Were you concerned during this time period with any danger that could come from Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not that concerned with Jezestica because all the other places that I indicated earlier were the true source of concern for me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: In your direct testimony you did testify that you had been told by people trying to reach Konjevic Polje about an army unit in Jezestica. Does that remain correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. As the civilians came to Konjevic Polje, probably on their way they passed by Jezestica and noticed this.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Are you aware of any battle that occurred in Jezestica in the month of August 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think the battle in Jezestica took place on the 8th of August between Nurif's fighters and Ejub Golic's men from the place of Cizmici, from Glogova.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's -- I think this needs some clarification because it seems -- it would mean that two Muslim factions, units, were fighting each other. As -- at least as the -- Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, he didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But therefore we need to have the correct translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we should ask him is that the case. Is that I think from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Witness -- let him say it, Ms. Vidovic. What did you actually answer to Ms. Sellers' question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said - and perhaps it was not interpreted correctly - Ejub Golic's group and Nurif Rizvanovic's group were attacking the area of Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you tell us whether Jezestica is actually a village that has two parts, an upper part and a lower part, of the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The question that you put to me before concerning Jezestica and whether I knew Jezestica, it had to do with the lower part of it. I went from Konjevic Polje towards Srebrenica, passing through the upper and the lower part of Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, for the attack, were Ejub Golic's men joined, participated, with Nurif Rizvanovic's men, did that attack take place in the upper part or the lower part of Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't really specify whether it was the upper or the lower part of Jezestica, but as far as I heard some ten Nurif's fighters joined Ejub Golic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And could you just tell us for clarification whether on August 8th, 1992, whether Jezestica was a Bosnian Serb -- primarily a Bosnian Serb hamlet or primarily a Bosnian Muslim hamlet.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jezestica was a Serb hamlet.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And also, do you know whether the battle or the attack on the 8th of August, whether at that point all Bosnian Serbs who lived in Jezestica left or whether some remained and some fled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, all the Serb villages around Kravica -- before the month of April 1992, the Serbs had left all those villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So it's your understanding that there were no Bosnian Serbs in Jezestica on the 8th of August, 1992. Is that what you're saying, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were Bosnian Serbs in Jezestica on that date, but there were no civilians. There were only military-aged men.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to ask the witness now to look at document ERN number 03729742. Your Honour, I would like to state that this is a document received by the Office of the Prosecutor regarding the Muslim attack on 8th August 1992 in the village of Jezestica, and we've gotten the document from a person -- I don't think I need to put the name on the record. I don't know who it is. But certainly the Trial Chamber once -- we can give both the Trial Chamber and the Defence and a copy of the MIF.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Sir, I want to draw your attention to a couple of things in this document, and one is that the document appears to be a statement taken by -- or given by a Mr. Rajko Jovanovic. It's signed Bratunac, 16th of August 1992. And it says in the very beginning: "Statement of Jovanovic, Rajko from Jezestica on the attack of the Muslim armed forces to that village on the 8th of August, 1992."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment. Yes, Mr. Jones.
